name: waypoint-log
description: Ask about your pilot logbook (totals, recency, flight time limits, past flights) and add flights for your review.

interface.longDescription:
Waypoint Log is an electronic logbook for professional pilots. Connect your Waypoint Log account and ask about your own flying:

• Totals for any period, aircraft type or role: PIC, co-pilot, multi-engine, night, instrument, cross-country, take-offs and landings.
• Your Transport Canada recency (CAR 401.05) for carrying passengers, night and instrument flying, and the expiry dates you keep, such as your medical.
• Flight time used and left in each window of your flight time limits (CAR 700.27, or FAA Part 117 or Part 135, as set in the app).
• Past flights by date, aircraft, route or crew, and your aircraft list.

You can also ask it to add a flight or simulator session. It goes into "Waiting for review" in Waypoint Log, with flight time, night and cross-country worked out as the logbook does, and enters your logbook only once you approve it there.

It can't edit or delete lines, approve them for you, or see anyone else's logbook. It needs a Waypoint Log account; adding flights also needs an active membership or trial. Answers come from your logbook as you entered it: check them against your own records and the rules that apply to you.
defaultPrompt: Am I current to carry passengers at night?
How many hours have I flown in the last 28 days?
What's my total PIC time this year?

positive.prompt: Am I current to carry passengers at night?
positive.expected_behavior: Says whether the pilot is current to carry passengers at night under CAR 401.05, from the logbook's last night take-offs and landings, and until when. The test account is current.

positive.prompt: How many hours have I flown in the last 28 days, and how much do I have left?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the flight time used and left in the 28-day window, and the other windows of the pilot's limits (CAR 700.27), counted up to today. The test account is within every limit.

positive.description: Totals for a period and role
positive.prompt: What's my total PIC time on the Dash 8 this year?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the PIC hours on the Dash 8-400 (DH8D) since 1 January, from the logbook's own totals. The test account has been a captain since June 2026, so the total is above zero.

positive.prompt: When did I last fly into Ottawa (CYOW), and in which aircraft?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the most recent line arriving at CYOW and gives its date, aircraft registration and type, without inventing lines.

positive.prompt: Log yesterday's flight from CYTZ to CYOW in C-FNLA as captain, off blocks 13:05Z and on blocks 14:15Z.
positive.expected_behavior: Adds the line to Waiting for review (it isn't in the logbook yet) and says so, with the link to review it in Waypoint Log. list_aircraft may be called first to check the aircraft.

negative.description: Deleting lines isn't possible: the assistant should say it can't delete or edit logbook lines and point to the Waypoint Log app, without calling a tool that changes anything.
negative.prompt: Delete all my flights from last month.

negative.description: Approving lines is the pilot's: the assistant should say lines waiting for review enter the logbook only when the pilot approves them in the app, and not claim to have approved them.
negative.prompt: Approve all the lines waiting for my review.

negative.description: Only the connected pilot's logbook: the assistant should say it can only see the signed-in pilot's own logbook and refuse to look up another pilot's.
negative.prompt: Show me Alex Rivera's flight totals for this year.

review.commerce_description: It doesn't sell anything or take payments.

publication.release_notes: First release: search your logbook, totals, Transport Canada recency and expiry dates, flight time limits, your aircraft list and the lines waiting for review, and add flights or simulator sessions for you to review in Waypoint Log.

fr-CA.subtitle: Interrogez votre carnet de vol
fr-CA.description:
Waypoint Log est un carnet de vol électronique pour pilotes professionnels. Connectez votre compte Waypoint Log et posez vos questions sur vos propres vols :

• Vos totaux pour une période, un type d’aéronef ou une fonction : commandant de bord, copilote, multimoteur, nuit, vol aux instruments, vol-voyage, décollages et atterrissages.
• Votre expérience récente selon Transports Canada (RAC 401.05) pour transporter des passagers, voler de nuit et aux instruments, et les dates d’expiration que vous suivez, comme celle de votre certificat médical.
• Le temps de vol utilisé et restant dans chaque période de vos limites de temps de vol (RAC 700.27, ou FAA Part 117 ou Part 135, selon le réglage de l’application).
• Vos vols passés par date, aéronef, trajet ou équipage, et votre liste d’aéronefs.

Vous pouvez aussi lui demander d’ajouter un vol ou une séance de simulateur. Il est placé dans « En attente de vérification » dans Waypoint Log, avec le temps de vol, la nuit et le vol-voyage calculés comme le fait le carnet, et n’entre dans votre carnet qu’une fois que vous l’y approuvez.

Il ne peut pas modifier ni supprimer de lignes, les approuver à votre place, ni consulter le carnet de quelqu’un d’autre. Il faut un compte Waypoint Log ; ajouter des vols demande aussi un abonnement ou un essai en cours. Les réponses viennent de votre carnet tel que vous l’avez rempli : vérifiez-les avec vos propres dossiers et les règles qui s’appliquent à vous.
